details:
Mars Guardian — An Interactive Martian Survival Guide

Mars Guardian is an interactive application designed to support future human exploration of Mars by making scientific information more accessible and useful.

Our project brings together information, discoveries, and scientific data from NASA's past and ongoing Mars missions. It allows users to explore the Martian surface, navigate high-resolution topographical maps, discover geological landmarks such as Jezero Crater and Gale Crater, and understand potential hazards astronauts may encounter.

The application focuses on four major challenges: radiation, dust storms, extreme temperatures, and difficult terrain. By presenting these challenges alongside possible survival strategies, Mars Guardian helps users understand the importance of preparation before human missions to Mars.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

Mars Guardian aims to make complex scientific information easier to explore and understand. It can support educational activities, improve awareness of Martian environmental risks, and help future researchers and explorers access relevant information when preparing for missions. As new discoveries and scientific data become available, the application could be expanded and improved to provide more detailed information and additional survival guidance.

Tools and Technologies:

Our team used Claude (Anthropic) as an AI-assisted coding tool to help with development, code generation, and troubleshooting. We also incorporated NASA's publicly available Mars exploration information and geographical data to support the application's scientific content. Our team guided the development process, project design, and overall functionality.

Creativity and Innovation:

The creative aspect of Mars Guardian is bringing Martian geography, scientific discoveries, environmental hazards, and survival knowledge together in one interactive platform. Instead of presenting information through text alone, users can explore the Martian surface and connect geographical locations with potential challenges.

Factors Considered:

Our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, usability, geographical detail, and the practical challenges of future human exploration. We focused on making the application informative, understandable, and capable of future expansion.

Our ultimate vision is to turn existing scientific knowledge into a useful resource that can contribute to safer, smarter, and better-prepared human exploration of Mars.
